concept.name: Partial autocorrelation
concept.definition: The correlation between a time series value and its value h periods earlier after removing the linear effect of all intervening lags (1 through h-1). It isolates the direct lag-h relationship that the ordinary autocorrelation confounds with indirect chains of correlation.
concept.intuition: If today's value correlates with last week's only because both depend on yesterday, the partial autocorrelation at lag 7 removes that indirect path and shows whether a genuine direct link remains.
concept.mechanics: Computed as the coefficient on the h-th lag in a regression of X_t on X_{t-1}, ..., X_{t-h}, or equivalently via Yule-Walker equations, Levinson-Durbin recursion, or Burg's estimator. For an AR(p) process the partial autocorrelation cuts off after lag p, making it a key tool for identifying autoregressive order.
concept.formula: pacf(h) = coefficient phi_hh in the regression X_t = phi_h1*X_{t-1} + ... + phi_hh*X_{t-h} + e_t.
concept.failure_modes: Sample estimates differ across estimation methods (Yule-Walker, OLS, Burg) especially in short samples; misspecified lag selection can make cutoff identification ambiguous. Non-stationary data invalidate the interpretation.
concept.misconceptions: That partial autocorrelation at lag h is just the autocorrelation at lag h 'cleaned up' numerically - it answers a different question (direct vs total dependence) and can differ in sign and magnitude.
concept.example: For an AR(2) process, the sample PACF shows significant spikes at lags 1 and 2 and near-zero values beyond lag 2, identifying the AR order.
